Choosing your career involves much more than just making a living. Life is one of the most important aspects of an individual. The quality of your work and work-life is profoundly influenced by your career and work life. It is, therefore, crucial to choose the right career path at the right time. Many working professionals have to experiment and select before finding the right career fit. Many people stay in jobs and careers they dislike because changing jobs and careers is a difficult process. Though they are ready for a change, they just aren’t aware of their options. A Career Counselor can provide you with advice when you’re unhappy with your career so that you can avoid leading an unsatisfying professional life. There is a massive need for career counseling for working professionals as many people decide their careers due to external pressures such as parental or peer pressure; and consequently, they end up regretting those decisions later on. Many factors determine a person’s success and happiness at work, such as superiors, co-workers, luck, job role, and interests, etc. When making career decisions, a Career Counsellor keeps these particular characteristics in mind. He/she first understands your unique situation before guiding you towards the best decision. Professionals who are interested in fast-tracking their careers or seeking inspiration for alternative career paths that might prove more fulfilling will most benefit from career guidance. This assessment aids in determining the need for reskilling and up-skilling. It profiles an individual based on their self-assessment of interests, work styles, abilities, values, knowledge, and skills. Several job families and occupation types will be recommended, along with information on education and skills required to pursue specific career paths. Individuals will also be given information on relevant education and skills for pursuing specific career paths or making conversion decisions. Using the assessment test, the candidate’s profile is compared with the profiles of successful people in similar careers to provide very accurate recommendations. Acquiring new skills It is common for professionals to experience situations when they feel they need to enhance their skills or education to move up the ranks or take on alternative roles. You should speak to a Career Counsellor if you find yourself in such a predicament, as taking a course usually means leaving your current job, which creates a high risk for your current employment. Furthermore, it might not be worth the risk, time, and money if the course is not optimal. You will be guided by your Career Counselor to explore the risks and benefits of further education based on your current situation. Your career advisor will help you identify your future goals, prospects, and suitability. You should consider the pros and cons of all your options with the assistance of a Career Counsellor before you make a final choice. Managing career setbacks Working professionals may have to deal with career setbacks. There can also be circumstances such as being laid off, laid off, or on maternity leave, etc. It is common for professionals to start over in these situations, which presents a challenge as well as an opportunity. After you’ve been laid off, there will be many decisions you will need to make, including whether to pursue the same career or a different one, the kind of company culture you would prefer, additional education or training you could take up before re-entering the workforce, etc. Having a Career Counsellor guide you through all these important decisions can make them easy and methodical. Your Career Counselor will evaluate your current situation after studying your personality. During the evaluation, he/she will determine whether you are a good fit in your past career and whether you should change careers. Changing your career It is common for many professionals to wonder whether they should change careers and pursue a career that matches their interests and personality. As a working professional, you have to make one of the most difficult decisions you’ll ever have to make. Change of career is a desire resulting from both dissatisfactions with your current job and a desire to move onto greener pastures of some other job. You need to be very cautious before making a decision that you’re seriously considering pursuing a dream career as a professional if you feel your true passion lies elsewhere. While making a career-related decision, a career counselor proves to be a helpful resource. Career counselors begin by getting to know your personality and strengths and weaknesses. So, he can determine whether the cause of your dissatisfaction is related to your job or your career. Counseling for Professionals: Why is it Important? The success and satisfaction of an individual at work are affected by many factors external to the workplace, including management, coworkers, job function, passions, and so on. You can factor these considerations into your decision-making by taking a career test and talking to a mentor. You must evaluate these factors against the responsibilities of the position to determine if you’re a good fit. With the rapid technological advances and the advent of artificial intelligence, many careers are becoming obsolete, these decisions have become even more critical today. Obtaining career counseling can assist you in making career changes, enhancing skills, taking up a graduate degree program, and finding a job after being terminated or laid off. As well as identifying opportunities that will be in demand in the future, a career mentor/coach can also identify how to prepare for the future. At present, there are very few online platforms that offer career advice to working professionals and help them make changes in their occupation or role using professional career assessment tests based on accurate and research-based information. Where to get the guidance? The 3RI Technologies platform has helped with career counseling for working professionals to choose their profession. Their career experts are highly recommended for answering any career questions you may have. Your psychometric assessment provides you with career guidance and career counseling. According to them, behavioral scientists can help resolve much of the student and professional confusion by using principles from behavioral science.
